Hey there, Grammaticus Nazicus here. 

I noticed you use the term [i]Unitas Senatus[/i], both of which are in the nominative case. This is technically okay, and someone reading the term may interpret it to mean "Unity Senate", but because both words are in the nominative case, the relationship between them isn't totally clear. It could be that rather than a Unity Senate, the name may be interpreted to just be a grouping of two variables, Unity [i]and[/i] Senate.

Therefore, I recommend adopting a genitive, which renders out to [i]Senatus Unitatis[/i] or [i]Unitatis Senatus[/i], which connects the two words better.
